Figure 6: Entanglement gap ∆ as a function of hidden dimensionality nh. Exact density matrix for nh ≤ 10; mean-field approximation for nh > 10. The mean-field approximation collapses the entanglement signal, indicating that exact density-matrix computation is necessary for detection.
Figure 5: Entanglement gap ∆ for each baseline model. Only the QBM achieves positive ∆; all classical models produce ∆ ≤ 0.
Figure 1: Entanglement entropy distributions for Self-Modeling (Type A), Instrumental (Type B), and Random agents. The gap ∆ = 0.381 is statistically significant (p < 0.001).

Table 5: Current release status against the deployment-level safety envelope. The frozen Phase I subset does not satisfy the full envelope and should be described as partial validation rather than a deployment-ready pass.

Table 6: Baseline comparison. ∆ > 0 indicates model separates Type A from Type B. Only the QBM achieves positive ∆; classical models fail to separate the two agent types with the mean-activation metric.
